fields.Frequency: Continuous (~5–8% of receipts have some discrepancy)
fields.Participants: DC Receiving, QC, Inventory Control, Vendor Mgmt

workflows.name: Inbound Receiving Damage & Shortage Identification & Documentation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-inspect of "inspects inbound delivery against PO/ASN" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "Receiving Clerk/QC documents damage" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-route of "route discrepancy to claim" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-499 (ensure controlled execution — Damage Identification, Documentation & Disposition (PA-90.1).)
- operational: mandatory photo + discrepancy capture at goods receipt
Pain Points / Risks: - **Evidence risk**: Damage not documented at receipt forfeits claim rights; mitigated by mandatory photo + discrepancy capture at goods receipt
System Touchpoints: - Goods receipt exception (links to VS-04); damage quarantine bin; discrepancy/claim case

steps.activity: Receiving Clerk inspects inbound delivery against PO/ASN; identifies visible damage, water damage, crushed packaging, or quantity shortage at goods receipt (links to VS-04)
Receiving Clerk/QC documents damage: photos, quantities damaged vs. received, carrier/seal condition, and discrepancy code in ERP goods-receipt exception
Inventory Control/Vendor Mgmt route discrepancy to claim (PA-90.2) or RTV (links to VS-32); place damaged units in damage quarantine pending disposition

fields.Participants: DC Ops, QC, Inventory Control, LP
fields.Trigger: Damage found at DC putaway, picking, or in-transit audit

workflows.name: In-Transit & DC Damage Identification, Quarantine & Classification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "log to damage case" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-assign of "assigns liability indicator for claim routing" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalates to VS-23 where fraud suspected" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-499 (ensure controlled execution — Damage Identification, Documentation & Disposition (PA-90.1).)
- operational: cause classification and LP review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-attribution risk**: DC handling damage wrongly charged to vendor/carrier; mitigated by cause classification and LP review
System Touchpoints: - Damage case; cycle count variance (links to VS-05); LP case linkage (links to VS-23)

steps.activity: DC staff identify in-house damage (putaway/pick handling, racking, contamination, pest, water) during cycle counts or pick; log to damage case
QC classifies damage cause: carrier-induced, vendor packaging, DC handling, environmental, or indeterminate; assigns liability indicator for claim routing
LP investigates patterns suggesting theft/concealment disguised as damage; secures evidence; escalates to VS-23 where fraud suspected

fields.Participants: Store Mgr, Receiving Clerk, Stock Associate, Customer Service
fields.Trigger: Store receives damaged goods or in-store damage occurs

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logs damage case with photos" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-route of "routes to claim, RTV, or write-off per disposition matrix" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinates goodwill/replacement where applicable" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-75 (detect and recover freight & receiving damage.)
- operational: mandatory damage-case logging; operational: damage-case logging
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-reporting risk**: In-store damage written off silently without recovery attempt; mitigated by mandatory damage-case logging
System Touchpoints: - Store damage case; goods receipt exception (links to VS-07); disposition matrix

steps.activity: Receiving Clerk/Stock Associate identifies DOA at store receiving or in-store damage (customer handling, drop, spill, weather in lumber yard); logs damage case with photos
Store Mgr classifies cause (carrier transit, DC pick error, in-store handling, customer-caused); routes to claim, RTV, or write-off per disposition matrix
Customer Service handles customer-caused damage (broken in-aisle) per store policy; coordinates goodwill/replacement where applicable (links to W3035)

fields.Participants: Inventory Control, DC/Store Staff, QC, Vendor Mgmt

workflows.name: Damage Documentation, Photographic Evidence & ERP Capture

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "capture standardized evidence" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "records damage event in ERP damage-case module" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validate evidence sufficiency for claim filing" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-499 (ensure controlled execution — Damage Identification, Documentation & Disposition (PA-90.1).)
- operational: standardized photo checklist and pre-claim validation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Evidence-quality risk**: Insufficient photos lead to claim denial; mitigated by standardized photo checklist and pre-claim validation
System Touchpoints: - Damage-case module with evidence attachments; image/document repository (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: DC/Store staff capture standardized evidence: photos (packaging, product, seal, carrier markings), quantities, SKU/lot, PO/ASN, carrier/waybill, witness
Inventory Control records damage event in ERP damage-case module: linked PO/GR, value at cost, liability indicator, evidence attachments
QC/Vendor Mgmt validate evidence sufficiency for claim filing (PA-90.2); flag incomplete evidence for remediation before claim submission

fields.Participants: Inventory Control, Merchandising, Vendor Mgmt, Finance

workflows.name: Damage Disposition Decision (Scrap / Return-to-Vendor / Salvage / Recondition)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Vendor Mgmt confirms vendor RTV authorization or salvage/liquidator acceptance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validates disposition value recovery vs." (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-499 (ensure controlled execution — Damage Identification, Documentation & Disposition (PA-90.1).)
- operational: disposition matrix and recovery-value check
Pain Points / Risks: - **Value-loss risk**: Suboptimal disposition (scrap when salvage viable); mitigated by disposition matrix and recovery-value check
System Touchpoints: - Disposition matrix; RTV/salvage order (links to VS-32); markdown pricing (links to VS-01)
Time Estimate: - Per event; faster for low-value, slower for high-value

steps.activity: Inventory Control/Merchandising decide disposition per matrix: scrap/destroy, return-to-vendor (RTV), sell-as-is at markdown, salvage to liquidator, or recondition/repair
Vendor Mgmt confirms vendor RTV authorization or salvage/liquidator acceptance; arranges reverse logistics (links to VS-32)
Finance validates disposition value recovery vs. scrap write-off; approves markdown/salvage pricing; ensures GL treatment correct (W3022)

fields.Participants: Finance, Inventory Control, DC/Store Mgr, Internal Audit

workflows.name: Damaged Inventory Quarantine, Write-Off & GL Posting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Finance posts inventory write-off to correct GL account" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System continuous audit of "Audit samples write-offs for control compliance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-499 (ensure controlled execution — Damage Identification, Documentation & Disposition (PA-90.1).)
- operational: approval matrix and Internal Audit sampling
Pain Points / Risks: - **Control risk**: Write-off used to mask theft; mitigated by approval matrix and Internal Audit sampling
System Touchpoints: - Inventory write-off/quarantine; GL posting; audit trail (links to VS-21)

steps.activity: Inventory Control moves dispositioned stock to write-off status; secures in quarantine pending destruction/RTV; prevents re-sale
Finance posts inventory write-off to correct GL account (damage/loss vs. COGS adjustment); captures cost, liability indicator, and pending-recovery flag
Internal Audit samples write-offs for control compliance; verifies approvals and recovery follow-through; investigates anomalies (links to VS-21)

fields.Participants: EHS, Quality, DC/Store Ops, Licensed Hazmat Vendor
fields.Trigger: Damaged hazardous/regulated goods (paint, solvents, chemicals, batteries, asbestos-adjacent)
fields.Volume: Subset of damage; hazardous categories ~8% of SKUs

workflows.name: Hazardous / Regulated Damaged Goods Handling & Disposal

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-post of "posts cost to damage case recovery" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-499 (ensure controlled execution — Damage Identification, Documentation & Disposition (PA-90.1).)
- operational: licensed vendor and manifest retention
Pain Points / Risks: - **Environmental/compliance risk**: Improper hazmat disposal triggers DENR penalties; mitigated by licensed vendor and manifest retention
System Touchpoints: - Hazmat storage/quarantine; SDS access (links to W1019); disposal manifest/retention (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: DC/Store staff isolate damaged hazardous goods in compliant hazmat storage; reference SDS (links to W1019); prevent spill/contamination exposure
EHS/Quality determine disposal method compliant with DENR/EHS rules and local ordinances; engage licensed hazmat disposal vendor
Hazmat Vendor disposes with manifest/certificate; EHS retains manifest per VS-24/VS-88 retention; Finance posts cost to damage case recovery

fields.Participants: Supply Chain Analytics, DC Ops, Store Ops, Vendor Mgmt, Merchandising

workflows.name: Damage Trend Analysis & Root Cause Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review top damage drivers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track reduction vs." (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-75 (detect and recover freight & receiving damage.)
- operational: trend visibility and scorecard consequences
Pain Points / Risks: - **Persistence risk**: Recurring damage not addressed; mitigated by trend visibility and scorecard consequences
System Touchpoints: - Damage analytics/dashboard (links to VS-28); vendor scorecard feed (links to VS-67)

steps.activity: Supply Chain Analytics produces damage trend dashboard: damage rate by vendor, carrier, lane, SKU category, DC, store, cause, and value
DC/Store Ops/Vendor Mgmt review top damage drivers; initiate corrective actions (packaging change, lane/lane carrier switch, handling training, racking fix)
steps.r: DC Ops / Store Ops / Vendor Mgmt

steps.activity: Merchandising/Vendor Mgmt feed damage trends into vendor scorecard and corrective action (links to VS-67); track reduction vs. targets
